purpose: Validate site-independent observation capture on newly added development domains without touching the held-out split.
notes: Vitacost and Staples initially returned 404 because their acquisition routes had changed; both templates were corrected and recaptured.
Wegmans, Save Mart, and Dollar General also changed search routes; browser-discovered templates recaptured all three with zero validation errors.
Etsy returned HTTP 403, while H-E-B returned an incomplete shell. These remain operational capture failures rather than zero-product pages.
Food Lion returned HTTP 403 in the additional development run and remains an operational capture failure.
The first all-development-domain pass separated 12 usable captures, 12 explicit site blocks, and 6 collector errors instead of treating missing observations as negative examples.
Walmart and Sam's Club exposed a DOM compatibility failure caused by relying on HTMLElement.dataset; standard Element attributes removed both collector errors on live reruns.

Kroger, Costco, Staples, and Office Depot repeatedly reset Playwright HTTP/2 navigation. Three bounded retries still failed, so these remain measured acquisition failures rather than silently omitted pages.
Visual inspection of a fresh Wegmans capture found and then verified fixes for scroll-coordinate misalignment and a late shallow cookie banner.

The heuristic candidate sampler found zero Staples cards even though the generic observation and bounded screenshot contained a product grid. Candidate cards therefore remain convenience artifacts and are not the learned card-discovery denominator.
No held-out domain was visited or inspected.
